FabricationProcess.comment: The elementals Pb, Ge, Te and Se with purities of 99.99% were used as starting materials. They were mixed  in the appropriate molar ratio of the Ge1xPbxTe0.5Se0.5 alloys with x = 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 in quartz  tubes and sealed under a vacuum of 3  103 Pa. The sam- ples were heated at 1273 K for 20 h for complete reaction  and homogeneity, and then slowly cooled to 873 K. They were held at 873 K for 4 h for solution treatment and then quenched in liquid nitrogen. The treated samples were then powdered by ball milling in a planetary ball mill using a hard stainless steel vial and balls at 200 rpm for 6 h. The weight ratio of balls to powders was kept at 20:1, and the mill vial was evacuated and then back filled with H2 atmosphere to prevent the powders from oxidizing during the milling process. The powders were consolidated into bulk by SPS at 773 K for 5 min under an axial pressure of 50 MPa.

Purity.comment: The XRD analysis shows that  the samples keep single rhombohedral GeTe-based super- saturated solid solution up to x = 0.3, while the samples  with x = 0.4 and 0.5 are composites containing the major rhombohedral GeTe-based supersaturated solid solution and a mixture of the minor NaCl-type PbTe-based and rhombohedral GeTe-based phases separated from the supersaturated solid solution without any additional phase arising from Se.

FabricationProcess.comment: Analytical purity Pb(NO3)2, AgNO3, SbCl3, and Na2TeO3 were used as the precursors. In a typical synthesis of LAST-18 nanopowders, about 40 mL deionized water was poured into a 100-mL beaker, and the beaker was placed on the plate of a magnetic force stirring device. The above precursors with the stoichiometric ratio of AgPb18SbTe20 were placed into the beaker one by one under constant stirring with a magnetic bar; after that, enough KOH and KBH4 were added into the beaker. The mixture was kept under stirring for 10 min before being poured into a 100-ml Teflon autoclave. Some deionized water was added into the autoclave until 85% of its volume was filled; subsequently, the autoclave was sealed, then placed into an oven, heated up to 180c and held at 180c for 20h. and cooled naturally to room temperature. Black precipitates at the bottom of the autoclave were collected and washed with deionized water and absolute ethanol in sequence for several times, and then separated by centrifugation for 5 min at 4000 rpm. The obtained black product was dried in vacuum at 70 1C for 6 h. The dried powders were loaded into a graphite crucible and then sealed in a quartz tube under 6.7 103 Pa before being flushed with argon for several times. The quartz tube was heated to 1173 - 1223K held at the temperature for 5 h, and then cooled to 723 K in 60 h, followed by naturally cooling to room temperature. Cylinder-like sample was obtained at the bottom of the graphite crucible. For the synthesis of PbTe powders and bulk samples, other conditions were the same as described above except that no salts of Ag and Sb were added during the hydrothermal synthesis process.

A pressure of 57 MPa was applied during the heating process.

ThermalMeasurement.comment: Thermal  diffusivity was measured for disk-shaped samples with a diameter of  12.7 mm and ~2 mm thickness by a flash diffusivity method (LFA 457  MicroFlash, Netzsch, Germany) from room temperature to 573 K under  Ar flow. The thermal conductivity t was calculated from measurements  of the thermal diffusivity, d, the specific heat, Cp, and the density ,  using the relationship: t = dp. The specific heat capacity, Cp, was  determined by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC 3, Mettler Toledo,  USA) and the volume bulk density, , was measured by the Archimedes  method.

ElectricalMeasurement.comment: The electrical conductivity, , and the Seebeck coefficient, S,  were measured in the temperature range from 100 to 900 K by the  standard four-probe and differential methods, respectively, using  laboratory-made system (Cryotel, Russia) in He2 atmosphere. The esti2mated errors in the Seebeck coefficient and the electrical conductivity  measurements are around 8% and 5%, respectively, and that of thermal  conductivity is estimated to be within 8%. Hall coefficient, RH, was  measured near room temperature by the Van der Pauw technique using  a galvano-magnetic properties measurement system (Cryotel, Russia) in  a magnetic field varied from  1 to 1 T and a constant electric current of  30 mA.
